findings.issue_text: All 6 lenses returned. Consolidated findings:
Missing validation evidence — no test/verification command output supplied for the branch (blocking; other 5 gates PASS)

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96 — `prisma.credential.update(...)` is called but `prisma` is never imported in this file; compile/runtime break (every other touched service imports `@calcom/prisma`)

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97 — `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)` stores the zod SafeParse *wrapper*, so `credential.key` is persisted as `{success:true,data:{...}}` instead of the token object. Was `googleCredentialSchema.parse(...)`. Corrupts every later `parse(credential.key)`

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:29 — helper returns the safeParse wrapper, not `.data`; contract is used inconsistently (salesforce/office365 unwrap `.data`, google does not). Should return `.data`

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11 — computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both stringify to the same literal `"[object Object]"`; the schema degenerates to `{access_token: string}`. The comments ("any numeric property is the expiry", "allow other properties") describe behavior the code does not implement; zod strips the rest, so expiry/scope/instance_url are dropped in credential-sharing mode

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:3-19 — the two branches return structurally unrelated types (raw `fetch` Response vs. whatever refreshFunction yields), untyped `() => any` with no return type and no `response.ok` check or `.json()`

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — `res?.data` assumes the Gaxios shape; in sync mode `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `Response` with no `.data` → `token.access_token` throws / persists undefined

packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177-200 — result asserted `as HubspotToken`; in sync mode it is a `Response`, so `expiresIn` is undefined → `expiryDate` becomes NaN and the Response object is written to `credential.key`; the catch at :203 only logs
packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:67-95 — still expects the Lark envelope (`data.data.access_token/refresh_expires_in`); a sync-endpoint response has no such shape

packages/app-store/office365video/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:61-95 — `key: responseBody` replaces the whole credential key; in sync mode the response has no `refresh_token`, so the stored refresh token is destroyed and the credential is permanently unrefreshable

packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:87-90 — still uses its own strict `webexRefreshedTokenSchema.safeParse` (requires scope/token_type/refresh_token/refresh_token_expires_in) rather than `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, so refresh always fails with credential sharing on

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:101-108 — the freshly refreshed token is persisted but the `jsforce.Connection` is still built from the stale `credentialKey.access_token`/`instance_url`; the refresh has no effect on the request path

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:30-59 — team credential creation checks only accepted *membership*, then `return`s before `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam`. That guard is only reached on the personal path where `state?.teamId` is falsy, so it always runs with `teamId: null` — a permanent no-op. Any ordinary team member can attach a Stripe/HubSpot/Salesforce/Webex/MSTeams credential to the whole team

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29 — if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset, a request with no header gives `undefined !== undefined` → false → the check passes and the endpoint is unauthenticated. Also non-constant-time comparison and no rate limiting. Once past it, the body's arbitrary `userId` lets a caller overwrite any user's credential keys
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 — no `req.method` guard; GET/PUT/DELETE all reach the create/update write path

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15 — the POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` carries no shared secret/signature/bearer and no scheme validation, yet its response is persisted as the user's OAuth credential. Anyone able to reach or MITM that endpoint can inject an attacker-controlled access_token

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/decodeOAuthState.ts:9 — unvalidated `JSON.parse(req.query.state)` cast to `IntegrationOAuthCallbackState`; no nonce/HMAC binding to the session, and `state.teamId` is attacker-chosen yet is the sole input deciding credential ownership above. Malformed state throws an uncaught SyntaxError → 500 in every callback. (Content is new files here, but this is a move of the pre-existing `_utils/{encode,decode}OAuthState.ts`; the sparse checkout can't confirm the originals — verify before treating as newly introduced)

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57-58 — `symmetricDecrypt(..., process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")` silently falls back to an empty key rather than refusing to run; the following `JSON.parse` is unguarded
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — `schema.parse` (not `safeParse`) with no try/catch: malformed body throws a ZodError → 500 with a stack instead of 400

packages/app-store/larkcalendar/api/callback.ts:98 — catch-branch `res.redirect(state?.returnTo ?? ...)` bypasses the `getSafeRedirectUrl()` used on the success path at :93 (open redirect). Pre-existing line; only the import changed

packages/app-store/stripepayment/api/callback.ts:51 — `res.redirect(returnTo || ...)` with `returnTo` from the parsed state and no `getSafeRedirectUrl` (open redirect). Pre-existing line; only the import changed

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:32-54 — check-then-insert with no unique index on (userId|teamId, appId): repeated OAuth callbacks create unbounded duplicate Credential rows; downstream `findFirst` then picks an arbitrary one

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-91 — read-then-branch instead of an atomic upsert, unbacked by a unique constraint; two concurrent deliveries both miss and both `create`. The comment "Can't use prisma upsert as we don't know the id" is the symptom of a missing `@@unique([userId, appId])`

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62 — `findFirst` with no `orderBy`, on a table where a user can legitimately hold several credentials for one appId (e.g. two Google accounts); which row gets overwritten is non-deterministic
apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:34 — `prisma.user.findUnique` with no `select`: pulls the entire user row (password hash, 2FA secret) just to test existence

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:40-54 — the `App` row is queried only to feed `app.slug` (already `reqBody.appSlug`) into the in-memory `appStoreMetadata` map; a redundant round-trip with two sources of truth that can disagree

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:73-80 — the update path writes `key` only: it never re-syncs `type` and never clears `invalid: true`, so a credential marked invalid by the googlecalendar `invalid_grant` handler stays invalid after fresh keys arrive

apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:60-88 — `userId` is required, so the team credentials that `createOAuthAppCredential` now creates with `teamId` cannot be synced; there is also no delete/revoke path

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts:42 — `select: { id: true, members: { select: { userId: true } } }` materializes every member row and never reads it; `select: { id: true }` suffices for an existence check

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-84 — unconditional token refresh on every `getClient()` with no expiry check (unlike every other adapter), against a hardcoded `https://login.salesforce.com` host that breaks sandbox/My Domain orgs
packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86 — `response.statusText !== "OK"` is an unreliable success test (HTTP/2 sends an empty statusText); use `response.ok`

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-26 — a missing refresh_token is silently replaced with the literal sentinel string `"refresh_token"`, which is then persisted and later sent to the provider as a real token

packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17 — unrelated change: redirect URI switched from `${appConfig.slug}` to a hardcoded `"zoho-bigin"` literal, desynchronizing it from config.json. Nothing in this PR requires it
packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-99 — an entire unconditional refresh + DB-write block added inside `getClient()`, well beyond the stated "use shared oauth utils" refactor

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75 — salesforce is presented as migrated but uses a raw `fetch`, never `refreshOAuthTokens`, so it bypasses the credential-sync endpoint the feature exists for

packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:263-268 — behavior change under a "refactor": the `console.error` zod diagnostics were deleted and the flow went from "log and continue with existing credentials" to "throw"; the residual `tokenResponse.success &&` guard is now dead

packages/app-store/googlecalendar/api/callback.ts:44, packages/app-store/office365calendar/api/callback.ts:68, packages/app-store/larkcalendar/api/callback.ts:70,79 — these adopt `decodeOAuthState` but keep the duplicated inline `prisma.credential.create`, so they get neither team-credential support nor the admin check, unlike hubspot/salesforce/webex/tandem/stripe/office365video

packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:92-94 and packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264 — dead branches: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws on failure, so `.success` can never be false at either call site

packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts:9-11 — `JSON.parse` immediately followed by `JSON.stringify` of the same value: a no-op that can only return its input, with an unvalidated type annotation and none of the integrity the name implies

(no file) — no tests anywhere in the changeset: no coverage for `parseRefreshTokenResponse`, `refreshOAuthTokens`, the `createOAuthAppCredential` team path, or the webhook (auth rejection, decryption failure, create vs. update)

Two caveats on verification scope: this checkout is sparse — only the 30 touched files exist — so cross-package references (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` from `@calcom/lib/constants`, `IntegrationOAuthCallbackState`, `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam`) and whether the old `_utils/{encode,decode}OAuthState,createOAuthAppCredential}.ts` files were deleted could not be checked against source. Everything else above was confirmed against the actual files.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a `fetch(...)` result (a `Response` object) when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` are truthy. In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code now does `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and (by implication of the previous implementation) will treat the returned value like a HubSpot token object (e.g., using `expiresIn`, `accessToken`, etc.). Unlike the Google/Office365 changes, HubSpot does not parse `Response` (no `await response.json()` / schema parsing), so in sync mode the value will be a `Response`, making token fields like `expiresIn` undefined and breaking expiry computation/refresh handling at runtime. The claim that the `Response` object is written to `credential.key` is not directly verifiable from the shown diff context, but the core type/behavior mismatch in sync mode is a real defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:67-95 — still expects the Lark envelope (`data.data.access_token/refresh_expires_in`); a sync-endpoint response has no such shape

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh flow now calls `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set (and `credential.userId` is truthy), `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the HTTP `Response` from the *sync endpoint* (POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), not from Lark’s `/authen/v1/refresh_access_token` API.

Immediately after, the code still does `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, this.log)`, which is designed to parse/validate Lark’s refresh token response shape (`RefreshTokenResp`, typically nested under Lark’s envelope). A sync endpoint response is documented in the diff to “only contain the access token and expiry date” and is therefore unlikely to match Lark’s expected envelope, making this a real correctness bug when sync is enabled for Lark.

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler authenticates solely via `req.headers[... ] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. If `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is truly unset (i.e., `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET === undefined`) and the request omits the header (so `req.headers[...] === undefined`), the comparison becomes `undefined !== undefined` which is `false`, so the 403 is not triggered and the request is accepted. After that, there is no other authorization: the caller can supply any `userId` and `appSlug`, and the code will `update`/`create` credentials for that user. The constant-time/rate-limiting notes are ancillary, but the unauthenticated access when the secret is unset and the resulting ability to overwrite arbitrary users’ credentials are real issues evident in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 — no `req.method` guard; GET/PUT/DELETE all reach the create/update write path

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: the new Next.js API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` exports a single `handler(req, res)` that performs auth checks and then parses `req.body` and writes to Prisma (`credential.update`/`credential.create`) without any `req.method` validation (e.g., `if (req.method !== "POST") ...`). As written, any HTTP method that reaches this handler (GET/PUT/DELETE/etc.) will proceed down the same create/update code path as long as headers/body are provided, so the finding is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-15 — the POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` carries no shared secret/signature/bearer and no scheme validation, yet its response is persisted as the user's OAuth credential. Anyone able to reach or MITM that endpoint can inject an attacker-controlled access_token

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts` the sync path (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId`) performs a `fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, { method: "POST", body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId, appSlug }) })` with no authentication material (no shared secret, signature, bearer token, etc.) and no validation that the endpoint is HTTPS/trusted. Call sites then treat the response as the refreshed token source and persist derived token fields back into the credential (e.g., Office365: `response = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` then `responseJson = await handleErrorsJson(response)` and `await prisma.credential.update(...)`). Therefore, if the endpoint or network path is attacker-controlled/compromised (including via an HTTP endpoint), attacker-supplied tokens could be written into the user's stored OAuth credentials.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57-58 — `symmetricDecrypt(..., process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")` silently falls back to an empty key rather than refusing to run; the following `JSON.parse` is unguarded

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler decrypts `reqBody.keys` via `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")` and immediately `JSON.parse(...)`s the result. adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:34 — `prisma.user.findUnique` with no `select`: pulls the entire user row (password hash, 2FA secret) just to test existence
